title: flow definition jitter_blocks has no upper bound: one accepted line names a mining request of up to 4,294,967,295 blocks, drawn per payment and sent as a single uncancellable `generate` RPC
description: `jitter_blocks: [min, max]` is accepted for any 1 <= min <= max, so a three-field flow definition can name a mining request of up to u32::MAX blocks (flow.rs:133, 166-176). Every draw is the argument to `ops::mine_and_resync(payer, jitter.next())` (flow.rs:645 per invoice, flow.rs:883 for a batch) and reaches zcashd's `generate` RPC as one call (ops.rs:436 -> node.rs:232); the only client-side bound is the 300 s response-read timeout (node.rs:122-125), which abandons the response and sends nothing that could cancel the work. Re-established independently in the approved sandbox: a serde-accepted definition `{"jitter_blocks":[1,4294967295],"jitter_seed":7}` drew 32 values with mean 1,791,207,489 and maximum 4,085,077,839 blocks in a single call, the first draw alone 1,789,459,390 — so the oversized request is the first payment's, not a tail event (matches the hunter's artifact draw-for-draw). What remains undecided from source or bounded local evidence is entirely node-side: zcashd's `generate` is not part of this repository, so whether it honours a count above the 32-bit signed range, whether it keeps generating after the client's socket closes, and what each block costs in time and disk on the shared host are unknown — and they decide the severity.
claimed_root_cause: Jitter::from_definition (flow.rs:166-176) bounds only the shape of the jitter range (1 <= min <= max; malformed ranges fall back to a fixed 3) and never bounds the work the range can name; the drawn value is passed unscaled to the node's `generate` RPC (ops.rs:436 -> node.rs:232), whose execution is not cancellable from the probe's side (the 300 s client read timeout at node.rs:122-125 abandons the response, not the server-side work; no cancel/shutdown path exists anywhere in the probe).

trace.description: the jitter range arrives as caller-controlled JSON (Option<[u32; 2]>, serde default, no validator); no upper bound is applied at deserialization, and u32::MAX is the largest count a definition can name
`Some([min, max]) if min <= max && min >= 1 => (min, max, None)` accepts the range verbatim (line 167); only malformed ranges are bounded, by the fixed-3 fallback at lines 168-176
`self.rng.gen_range(self.min..=self.max)` yields a count up to 4,294,967,295; recorded in jitter.drawn (line 195) and cast to u64 (line 196), never clamped
`ops::mine_and_resync(payer, jitter.next())` runs after every payment (batch path: one call at flow.rs:883 in settle_batch)
the drawn count becomes the one argument of `node.generate(blocks)` (mine_and_resync, ops.rs:433)

the count is the single parameter of the zcashd `generate` RPC, sent as one raw HTTP request (body at node.rs:80-92); this client's only bound is the 300 s read timeout at node.rs:122-125, which abandons the response without sending any cancellation

evidence.description: the acceptance rule for jitter_blocks: min <= max and min >= 1 — no maximum magnitude, no relationship to chain height or run length; the definition-level validation block (flow.rs:253-297) never inspects the field
per-invoice mining call (batch equivalent flow.rs:883); the draw is the only thing controlling the number of blocks

the 300 s response-read timeout (connect is bounded at 30 s, node.rs:94): on timeout the client errors and closes the request whose server-side work continues by construction; no cancel/shutdown path exists in the probe (grep: the only 'kill' is the payer grant's unrelated --kill-file)

observed locally (verifier-19, approved sandbox, disposable copy restored to HEAD sha afterwards): definition jitter_blocks [1,4294967295] + jitter_seed 7 is accepted and 32 draws give max 4,085,077,839, mean 1,791,207,489, first draw 1,789,459,390 — matching agents/hunter-inputs/artifacts/check-jitter-draw.txt draw-for-draw; raw run: agents/verifier-19/artifacts/check-jitter-independent.txt. Correction to the hunter's arithmetic: the 32-draw mean is 1.79e9, not ~1.9e9. Also: [4294967295,4294967295] is accepted and draws exactly 4,294,967,295; malformed [2,1] falls back to fixed 3

the composite action wraps the gate in `timeout "$GATE_TIMEOUT"` (default 2700 s; 124 -> exit 2 at action.yml:122-124), and the gate reaches this same Jitter path via gate.rs:133 flow::run_recording — it bounds the probe's own exposure but sends nothing to the node, so the mining it asked for is unaffected by killing the probe

blockers: zcashd's `generate` implementation is not part of this repository (harness/docker-compose.yml pins the electriccoinco/zcashd image), so whether it honours a block count above the 32-bit signed range, and whether generation continues after the client's 300 s read timeout closes the socket, cannot be decided from source or from bounded local evidence — and that answer decides whether the effect is a rejected request, a hung RPC, or a host-level drain.

Per-block mining cost and disk growth are runtime facts of the running node: this run's protocol puts the rig's containers and host ports (zanary-zcashd, 18232/18233) out of bounds, the approved sandbox is --network=none with rust:1-slim only, and image pulls are not permitted — so no node can be started or reached to measure them.

The named work is finite (<= 4,294,967,295 blocks per call, one call per payment), so the maximum is bounded in principle; what stays unknown is the node's actual rate and whether that work survives client abandonment, which is what a severity statement would need.

validation_plan.local: Runnable only where a disposable node is allowed (not this run's sandbox, which has no node and no network). Create a NEW throwaway container from the locally pinned zcashd image — never the harness's compose project, no published host ports, its own volume — on a fresh container-internal network, and point ZANARY_NODE_RPC_URL at it from a client on that same network. Then through the target's own code: (a) call NodeRpc::generate with a small count (e.g. 2,000) and confirm one request is emitted and honoured (getblockcount advances by 2,000); (b) start one generate with a count large enough to outlast a forced abort (or SIGKILL the probe process mid-call) and poll getblockcount from inside the node container to see whether height keeps climbing after the client socket closes; (c) record the node volume's size before and after. Bound the whole check to a couple of minutes, never request the drawn ~4.29e9, and delete the container and its volume afterwards.
validation_plan.deployment: The rig owner (not this verifier) repeats (b)/(c) on a DISPOSABLE node built from the harness image to measure per-block time and disk growth for a bounded count, then extrapolates the cost of 4,294,967,295 blocks arithmetically instead of letting the real request run — a giant `generate` against a retained rig volume could fill the disk, so the full draw must never be executed against shared rig state. If the end-to-end path must be shown, run the gate once with a definition jitter_blocks [1, 4294967295] against a throwaway node whose volume is discarded, guarded by the node's disk headroom and the action's 2700 s timeout, and watch getblockcount in a bounded window afterwards.
